statement: A cake looks the same on both sides of a line through its middle. It has 4 cherries on the left side and 1 cherry on the line. How many cherries does it have?

choices.misconception: I only counted the cherries on the left side of the line.
I added the cherry on the line to the left side but forgot the right side.
I doubled the 4 cherries on the left but forgot the cherry on the line.
I doubled the cherry on the line too, as if it had a partner on the other side.

hints: What does the right side of the cake look like?
Each cherry on one side has a matching cherry on the other side. A cherry sitting on the line is its own match, so it is counted only once.
The right side has 4 cherries, the same as the left. Add the left side, the right side and the one cherry on the line.

solutions.reliable: The right side matches the left side, so it also has 4 cherries. That makes $4 + 4 = 8$ cherries off the line. The cherry on the line has no partner, so add it once: $8 + 1 = 9$. The idea to keep: in a symmetric picture, things off the line come in pairs, and things on the line are counted once.

whyOnTest: Symmetry doubles everything off the mirror line but not what sits on it, and that one detail is where young solvers slip.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
